title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q), or more generally a candidate automorphism Θ, acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0) of U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}. Here I_0 is a set of (probably tangential) base points, and the action fixes the vertices. The previous page asked when such a Θ comes from some u ∈ Γ. Its necessary condition reads: for every finite étale cover f: C → U_{0,3} defined over a number field K, with I = f^{-1}(I_0), the action must lift to Π̂_1(C, I) and be the identity on vertices. In a weakened form, only some power Θ^n is required to lift.

This page. Grothendieck renames these conditions from 'prolongeabilité' to (probably) 'inductibilité'. He then adds a further condition. Suppose C maps to a curve X, typically a partial or full compactification of C, or more generally any morphism C → X under which the base points I map into X. Then the lifted action on Π̂_1(C, I) must pass to the quotient Π̂_1(X, I).

He states this precisely in terms of one base point x_0 ∈ I. The image of the Γ-action on π̂_1(C, x_0) ⊂ π̂_1(U_{0,3}, f(x_0)) must stabilise the kernel of π̂_1(C, x_0) → π̂_1(X, x_0). This kernel is the normal subgroup generated by the inertia (loops) at the filled-in punctures. He remarks that the condition at one x_0 implies it at all other x_i ∈ I. This holds because the lifted action is an automorphism of the groupoid Π̂_1(C, I): kernels at different vertices are conjugate by paths in C, and Θ sends paths in C to paths in C.

He then turns to the lifting question itself: when does Θ lift to Π_1(C, I)? He starts a groupoid lemma. Let 𝒯' → 𝒯 be a homomorphism of connected groupoids that is injective on π_1. Then 𝒯' is equivalent to a covering of 𝒯, though not necessarily itself a covering. The next page completes the lemma. 𝒯' embeds as a full subgroupoid of a genuine finite covering 𝒯̃. An automorphism Θ of 𝒯 fixing x_0 lifts to 𝒯̃ fixing x_0' if and only if the subgroup π_0' = im π_1(𝒯̃, x_0') ⊂ π_0 = π_1(𝒯, x_0) is Θ-stable. The fibres are then given by Ob 𝒯̃_{x_i} = H_{x_i,x_0} ∧^{π_0} π_0/π_0'.

Purpose. The page belongs to a programme of characterising the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) inside the automorphisms of the profinite (tangential-base-point) groupoid of U_{0,3}. The conditions are compatibility with the whole tower of finite étale covers and with the 'filling-in' (compactification) maps of those covers.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that kernel-stability at one x_0 implies it at all x_i ∈ I tacitly uses that Θ has already been lifted to a groupoid automorphism of Π̂_1(C, I) fixing vertices. Without the lift it would not follow.
The relation between 'Γ' and 'Θ' is fluid on the page. He writes 'l'action de Γ' where the condition is really on the candidate Θ (or Θ^n); for a genuine Galois element the condition is automatic.

ideas.what: Necessary conditions on an automorphism Θ of π̂_1 (or Π̂_1 with tangential base points) of P^1 \ {0,1,∞} to come from Gal(Q̄/Q). The conditions are: liftability to every finite étale cover C, and compatibility with the quotients π̂_1(C) → π̂_1(X) for compactifications or partial compactifications X of C (stability of the kernel generated by inertia).
ideas.modern_name: Cover-plus-filling-in conditions characterising G_Q inside Aut/Out of π̂_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}): Ihara's question / Oda–Matsumoto conjecture ('I/OM'), anabelian characterisation of G_Q via the tower of covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (question, 1980s); Oda–Matsumoto (conjecture, 1990s); F. Pop (finite-tripod variants of I/OM, 2010s); related work by Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki, André
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses determining Γ through the Teichmüller tower and GT-type conditions. This specific cover-plus-compactification kernel-stability formulation is not in the Esquisse as far as I know.

ideas.what: Lemma: a homomorphism of connected groupoids injective on π_1 identifies the source with a full subgroupoid of a genuine covering. An automorphism fixing a base vertex lifts to the covering iff the corresponding subgroup is stable, with fibres given by the contracted product H_{x_i,x_0} ∧^{π_0} π_0/π_0'.
ideas.modern_name: Covering theory of groupoids (Galois correspondence for groupoid coverings, lifting criterion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; R. Brown, P. J. Higgins (groupoid coverings), going back to SGA1-style Galois theory
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA1 (Galois categories); groupoid version not stated there in this form

ideas.what: Renaming 'prolongeabilité' conditions as conditions of 'inductibilité' (lifting/induction to covers), plus a weakened form with Θ replaced by a power Θ^n.
ideas.modern_name: Weak liftability (up to finite index / powers) to the tower of covers

missed.claim: As early as about 1978–81, Grothendieck formulates two conditions on a candidate automorphism of the profinite groupoid of P^1 \ {0,1,∞} with tangential-type base points: liftability to all finite étale covers C defined over number fields, and preservation of the kernels of π̂_1(C) → π̂_1(X) for compactifications X. These are necessary conditions for it to be Galois. This anticipates the shape of Ihara's question and the Oda–Matsumoto / Pop 'I/OM' framework, where G_Q is recovered as automorphisms compatible with covers and filling-in maps.
missed.quote: on trouve une condition supplémentaire, quand on de plus des morphismes Π̂_1(C,I)→Π̂_1(X,I), que celui-ci passe au quotient - ce qui s'exprime très exactement par la condition que pour un x_0∈I, l'action de Γ sur π̂_1(C,x_0)⊂π̂_1(M_{0,3},f(x0)) laisse stable le noyau de π̂_1(C,x_0)→π̂_1(X,x_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority rather than a new theorem: an explicit early formulation of the cover-plus-compactification compatibility conditions, at groupoid level with several base points. It also contains the weakening to a power Θ^n, a variant that might be of interest for 'up-to-finite-index' versions of I/OM.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck explicitly formulating, at groupoid level with many base points, the lifting-to-covers and kernel-stability-under-compactification conditions on Galois-type automorphisms. This is close in spirit to the later Ihara / Oda–Matsumoto / Pop I/OM line of work. That he thought along these lines is broadly known from the Esquisse, so it is notable but not shocking; the groupoid lemma itself is routine.
transcription_corrections: 'Nous sentons [?] bien [?]' is unclear in the image; the reading is uncertain.
'il faut mieux dire d'irréductibilité' more likely reads 'd'inductibilité' (conditions of lifting/induction to covers), which fits the context.
'avec Θ remplacé par un Θ^-' should be 'par un Θ^n' (a power of Θ, as on the previous page).
'qui celui-ci passe au quotient' should read 'que celui-ci passe au quotient'.
In 'π̂_1(M_{0,3}, f(x_0))', the handwriting shows U_{0,3} (or M_{0,3}); either way it denotes P^1 \ {0,1,∞}.
In the lemma, the groupoids are written with script 𝒯 (𝒯' → 𝒯), as on the next page, not 𝒞.
'Π_1(C,I)' in 'possibilité de relever l'action de Θ à Π_1(C,I)' is written without a hat on the page.
